newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Lebed urges ill Yeltsin to step down.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed urges ill Yeltsin to step down.

text.p: Alexander Lebed, Boris Yeltsin's ousted national security adviser, on Wednesday urged the Russian president to resign following his admission to hospital with first signs of pneumonia.
"Our country is headed by a very sick and elderly man. He needs to retire," Lebed, one of Russia's most popular politicians and a likely presidential candidate, told Ekho Moskvy radio.
"Let him choose one thing -- either work or life. In this situation one should choose one's life," said Lebed, who was sacked by Yeltsin last October.
Despite his remarks, Lebed said: "Of course, he will remain."
Yeltsin brought Lebed into the Kremlin after the latter finished a strong third in the first round of last year's presidential election.
Lebed helped Yeltsin win the runoff on July 3 but immediately clashed with other Kremlin officials and was later accused by Yeltsin of having presidential ambitions.
Since his dismissal, Lebed has started moves to form his own political movement with a view to running in the next presidential election -- due in the year 2000.
Yeltsin, who had a heart bypass operation on November 5, was admitted to Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital on Wednesday evening.
